transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recorders: Fireflies.ai
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.example.com/horizonlink-integration-deck (private), runbook draft: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/hzlnk-draft

Summary:
- Handoff / alignment for marketplace listing and joint runtime orchestration between Redwood and HorizonLink.
- Focus areas: onprem/VPC connector, KMS integration, canary deploys, fallback routing, quantization tradeoffs, telemetry and SLA targets.
- Agreed next steps: run benchmarks in HorizonLink staging, share helm chart and runbook, finalize canary policy.

Topics covered:
- Deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs HorizonLink-managed connector
- Networking: VPC peering, private endpoints, subnets, security groups
- Key management: KMS/HSM integration and envelope encryption
- Model variants: quantized vs FP16, fallback model routing policies
- Observability: per-route latency, token-level cost, tracing hooks
- Compliance: SOC2 logs, audit trail retention and RBAC

Action items (recorded in notes as strings above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: ok everyone thanks for joining, um we figure we'll run through the integration checklist and then handoff the se work to Jared and Lina, cool?
[00:18] Samir Rao: yeah thanks Maya, from HorizonLink side we're mainly trying to understand how the connector will sit in our marketplace listing flow and what parts Redwood needs from our infra team, like VPC endpoints, KMS keys, etc.
[00:30] Jared Kim: great, I'll start with a rough topology. The connector runs as a containerized adaptor in your VPC, it accepts requests from your marketplace gateway over a private endpoint, it then talks to the Redwood control plane for model catalog and metrics; data plane traffic stays in VPC where possible.
[00:47] Priya Nandakumar: quick q — do we need to open egress to Redwood's hosted inference or can everything be routed through our dedicated link?
[00:55] Lina Gomez: you can pin to Redwood Dedicated or use a HorizonLink-managed private connector. For fully air-gapped onprem you'll run the private deployment package; network egress only required for control plane unless you choose hosted inference.
[01:12] Oliver Chen: and that private deployment supports our HSM for key unwrap? Dana, can you confirm the compliance ask?
[01:20] Dana Ruiz: yes we need envelope encryption where customer keys live in our HSM; audit logs must show key usage and be retained 12 months for now. SOC2 baseline.
[01:28] Jared Kim: our Private package integrates with customer KMS via standard grpc endpoints and supports HSM-backed keys, we emit audit events to stdout which you can forward to your SIEM; the runbook has details on logging paths and retention configuration.
[01:41] Samir Rao: great. On models — our marketplace will want to advertise a low-cost quantized model as default but fallback to a higher-quality FP16 in case of quality regressions. How do you recommend routing?
[01:53] Ethan Ross: we've seen a common pattern: route 95% of traffic to quantized variant with a canary 5% to FP16 for selected prompt sets — also use Redwood Optimize to monitor quality regressions via eval sets and roll back automatically.
[02:08] Priya Nandakumar: the quantization we're talking about is int8? Any known latency improvements?
[02:13] Jared Kim: yes int8 and 4-bit variants are supported depending on model; latency improvements typically 1.6x-3x per-token and large cost savings but there are accuracy tradeoffs. We'll share benchmark data.
[02:26] Maya Patel: note we'll include per-route token cost and latency in the marketplace listing — HorizonLink can show a pricing SKU for quantized and for high-accuracy.
[02:36] Oliver Chen: on the deployment side, what's the recommended canary rollout policy? We need something that works with our CI/CD.
[02:43] Lina Gomez: typical is staged canary: 1) initial 1% traffic for 1 hour with smoke tests, 2) increase to 5% for 24h with eval metric monitoring, 3) 25% then full. Redwood can abort and fallback to previous variant or route to hosted fallback.
[03:00] Samir Rao: fallback to hosted? We prefer not to send customer data off-prem.
[03:05] Jared Kim: totally understood — fallback options are configurable: you can fallback to a different on-prem variant or to a sandboxed hosted model if you accept that policy. We'll document the policy choices in the runbook.
[03:18] Dana Ruiz: on SSO/SSO integrations — we need SAML for the management console, and RBAC so marketplace ops can't change customer keys.
[03:26] Maya Patel: Redwood supports SAML/SSO and granular RBAC; we can show an example attribute mapping.
[03:33] Priya Nandakumar: for the helm chart, can it precreate K8s secrets from the KMS rotation? We need automated rotation without human intervention.
[03:41] Lina Gomez: yes the chart supports secret-provider-interfaces to fetch keys at boot and rotate; we also support a KMS sync controller if you want a continuous reconcile.
[03:50] Oliver Chen: networking — what's the minimal port set? Also NAT vs no NAT?
[03:55] Jared Kim: minimal is outbound HTTPS to control plane (443) if using hosted control. For pure private deployments no external egress is required; the data plane ports are configurable, usually gRPC 8443 between connector and model workers.
[04:07] Samir Rao: can we lock that to internal subnets?
[04:10] Jared Kim: yes recommend private subnets only with SG rules allowing only your gateway IPs.
[04:15] Maya Patel: ok switching to observability — what metrics are important to you?
[04:19] Priya Nandakumar: per-route p95 latency, token cost, error rates, and traces for slow requests. Also KV cache hit rates — we rely on caching for prompt prefixes.
[04:29] Jared Kim: Redwood emits per-token latency, token count, route labels, and KV cache stats. You can forward to Prometheus or ingest into your telemetry.
[04:37] Dana Ruiz: audit logs, too — who called what model and when. We need immutable logs.
[04:42] Lina Gomez: runbook includes examples for forwarding logs to S3 or your SIEM with signed digests for immutability.
[04:49] Samir Rao: bench plan — we want to run a smoke bench that measures end-to-end p50/p95, cold vs warm cache, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:58] Ethan Ross: Jared will provide a bench script. We recommend test scenarios: 1) cold start sequence, 2) steady-state streaming at 20rps, 3) burst to 200rps to validate autoscaling.
[05:12] Oliver Chen: autoscaling — do we control the policy? If we're hosting the connector we want to set CPU thresholds and token queue sizes.
[05:19] Lina Gomez: yes the connector exposes autoscale knobs; for Redwood Dedicated you'll also get platform autoscaling but we can expose those knobs in the helm values.
[05:27] Priya Nandakumar: security — any native encryption in transit between connector and workers?
[05:31] Jared Kim: mTLS is supported end-to-end; we recommend cert rotation via the same KMS mechanism.
[05:38] Dana Ruiz: what about pen tests? We need to include the connector in our annual pentest scope.
[05:41] Maya Patel: that's fine — we can supply an architecture diagram and remediation contacts; we also have vulnerability reports we can share under NDA.
[05:51] Samir Rao: competitive question — CloudX Endpoints demands static IP whitelisting, do you support static egress?
[05:57] Jared Kim: yes static egress or NAT ranges are supported; we've done static IP NAT gateways for customers who require it.
[06:05] Priya Nandakumar: let's talk about packaging for the marketplace listing — we want a single-tenant deployable option and a managed option.
[06:11] Ethan Ross: we can produce two SKUs in the listing: HorizonLink-managed connector (with SLA) and self-hosted on your infra. Listing will include performance profile and a suggested price delta for quantized vs FP16.
[06:23] Oliver Chen: required documents for listing — what do you need?
[06:26] Maya Patel: architecture diagram, runbook, compliance attestation, helm chart, and a short deployment guide. We'll also want a short 2-slide performance summary.
[06:36] Dana Ruiz: attestation — what's your SOC2 coverage?
[06:38] Maya Patel: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and has ISO 27001 in progress. We'll share the compliance pack; for HorizonLink listing we'll include the relevant control mappings.
[06:47] Priya Nandakumar: for the bench we also need model seed prompts — can we reuse the public eval set or do you want a HorizonLink-specific set?
[06:54] Ethan Ross: start with our public eval set for baseline, then add HorizonLink-specific prompts to capture your UX. That will be part of the Optimize integration.
[07:03] Samir Rao: IAM and permissions — can we ensure marketplace ops cannot rotate customer keys?
[07:07] Lina Gomez: yes via RBAC mapping on the Red-wood control plane; only KMS-admin role can rotate keys. We'll show a sample SAML mapping.
[07:15] Oliver Chen: is there rate limiting built into the connector or at the control plane?
[07:20] Jared Kim: both; connector enforces per-tenant throttles and the control plane applies global quotas.
[07:25] Maya Patel: brief pause — I also want to call out quantization caveats: for certain safety prompts we recommend pinning to FP16. We'll document how to add rule-based routing for those prompts.
[07:36] Dana Ruiz: perfect. Any legal/procurement notes? We have standard marketplace T&Cs that require a 90 day data deletion window after contract termination.
[07:45] Maya Patel: Redwood can comply, we expose retention configs; we'll add deletion playbook in the runbook.
[07:51] Priya Nandakumar: ok, on benchmarks — Oliver will provide subnet info and we'll schedule the bench run.
[07:56] Oliver Chen: yes will do that.
[08:00] Jared Kim: I'll summarize the bench config: model A quantized int8, model B FP16 baseline; traffic patterns: cold, steady 20rps, burst 200rps; record p50/p95, token cost, cache hit rate.
[08:14] Samir Rao: time-wise we want to ship a beta listing in Q2 FY28; what's realistic?
[08:20] Ethan Ross: if bench goes well and security checklist cleared, beta listing in ~6-8 weeks is reasonable.
[08:27] Maya Patel: ok we'll target that. Next, handoff specifics — Jared, Lina you'll be point for the SE work, Maya for commercial and packaging.
[08:36] Jared Kim: noted.
[08:38] Lina Gomez: I'll draft the canary policy and helm notes.
[08:42] Dana Ruiz: I'll get an initial list of compliance items.
[08:45] Priya Nandakumar: I'll coordinate infra resources.
[08:48] Maya Patel: awesome. Any open questions?
[08:51] Oliver Chen: quick one — does Redwood provide an offline mode for inference if the control plane is unreachable?
[08:56] Jared Kim: private deployments include an offline runtime mode: model workers can serve without control plane for N days; you need to seed the model artifacts and keys. We'll add docs.
[09:08] Samir Rao: that's important for us.
[09:11] Maya Patel: ok wrapping up, recap of next steps: Jared to send bench script and helm sample, Lina to send canary draft, Maya to share listing checklist and compliance pack. We'll reconvene after bench results.
[09:24] Ethan Ross: I'll propose a time for the bench review.
[09:27] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via the shared doc and I'll email the runbook link.
[09:33] Priya Nandakumar: thanks all.
[09:35] Meeting end.
